title: Conformance litmus for hosted endpoint behaviors and launch safeguards
creator: Ava Chen
description: Objective: Define a PRD for a deterministic conformance "litmus" that validates behavioral contracts for hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) and ship an automated pre-launch gating pipeline. Background: We repeatedly see regressions when model variants or runtime kernel changes are introduced. Existing launch checklists focus on infra readiness and basic smoke tests; we need a lightweight but rigorous behavioral layer that ensures semantic/quality invariants before traffic ramps. Scope: - Author canonical prompt suites and evaluation harness per endpoint type - Define pass/fail thresholds focused on regressions and non-deterministic noise tolerance - Integrate litmus into CI and deployment gating (canary block) - Provide observability hooks to link failed litmus cases to triage runbooks Out of scope: full eval platform replacement, new model architecture research, offline large-scale evaluation jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical prompt suites exist for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank with at least 40 representative cases each (edge cases + common patterns)
A deterministic scoring function and noise-tolerant threshold is documented and approved (e.g. embedding cosine delta < 0.03 baseline), including rationale for thresholds
A CI job (litmus-run) executes the suites against a canary deployment and fails the pipeline on regression above thresholds
Runbook exists that maps litmus failures to owner(s), triage steps, and rollback criteria
Dashboard shows rolling pass-rate and per-test failure taxonomy; alerts configured for sustained degradation (>5% failing over 30m)
API contracts validated for backward compatibility: no breaking schema changes to request/response surfaces used by customers in last 6 months
success_metrics: 0 production-quality regressions attributable to runtime or model variant swaps for the first 90 days after launch
Litmus CI coverage: 95% of PRs that change runtime/model selection execute litmus-run before merge
Mean time to detection for behavioral regressions reduced from >24h to <30m (from alert trigger)
Canary abort rate due to litmus failures under 2% after stabilization
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize PRD and canonical prompt suites with input from Eng, Applied ML, DX
Week 1: Build litmus-run CI job and baseline against current production models
Week 2: Integrate litmus into canary pipeline (block on failures) and create runbook
Week 3: Dashboard and alerting go-live; run chaos scenarios to validate noisiness and thresholds
Week 4: Soft launch (internal teams) for 7 days, iterate thresholds, then public rollout with staggered traffic increase
tasks: PM: curate representative prompt cases for each endpoint type and collect labeled expected outputs (PM-req-01)
Eng: implement litmus-run job and CI integration (ENG-setup-litmus)
Applied ML: propose scoring functions and baseline deltas for embeddings and responses
DX/Design: add a quick triage UI in Console to inspect failed litmus cases
SRE/Infra: ensure canary pipeline can be blocked by litmus job and provide capacity for runs
Security: review data retention for prompt samples and ensure no PII saved in litmus artifacts
notes: Design decision: favor small focused suites (40 cases) over large brittle corpora to speed CI runs
Trade-off: tight thresholds reduce false negatives but can increase canary aborts; we will iterate from conservative to stricter after 1 week of internal runs
Consideration: embeddings drift across quantization changes — baseline should be tied to representative model variants (quantized fp16/int8)
